# provider setup

Generated from `ronin.providers.registry.ADAPTERS` and
`ronin.providers.openai_compat.KNOWN_BASE_URLS`. Every provider on this page has a
real implementation in this checkout; nothing is listed aspirationally.

Config is TOML because `tomllib` is in the standard library and the file is
hand-edited. Two sections: `[roles]` maps a *role* to a model name, and
`[models.<name>]` says what that model is.

The rule the role system encodes: **never burn the main model on grep triage.** A
subagent summarizing forty search hits and a compaction pass rewriting history are
both mechanical work, so the role is part of the request and the model is part of the
config. `Router.for_subagent()` and `Router.for_compaction()` take no role argument
at all, so those two callers cannot get it wrong by forgetting one.

A key is never written in the config file — `api_key_env` names an environment
variable instead, because a config file with a secret in it ends up in a git history.

## roles

| role | what routes here |
|---|---|
| `main` | the session's own reasoning and code writing. Required. |
| `plan` | plan mode, where nothing may mutate. Falls back to `main`. |
| `fast` | subagents and history compaction. Falls back to `main`. |

`main` is required. A config that omits `fast` routes mechanical work to the main model and still *works* — falling back beats crashing mid-session — and the fallback is visible in the ledger, where a `fast` row naming the main model is the signal to fix the config.

## providers with a real adapter

| `provider =` | wire protocol | default base url | key from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anthropic` | Anthropic messages API | — | `api_key_env` |
| `mlx` | in-process, no HTTP at all | — | no key; the weights are on disk |
| `kimi` | Moonshot (OpenAI-shaped, vendor quirks handled) | — | `api_key_env` |
| `moonshot` | Moonshot (OpenAI-shaped, vendor quirks handled) | — | `api_key_env` |
| `deepseek` | OpenAI chat-completions | `https://api.deepseek.com/v1` | `api_key_env`, or nothing for a keyless local server |
| `groq` | OpenAI chat-completions | `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1` | `api_key_env`, or nothing for a keyless local server |
| `llamacpp` | OpenAI chat-completions | `http://localhost:8080/v1` | `api_key_env`, or nothing for a keyless local server |
| `lmstudio` | OpenAI chat-completions | `http://localhost:1234/v1` | `api_key_env`, or nothing for a keyless local server |
| `ollama` | OpenAI chat-completions | `http://localhost:11434/v1` | `api_key_env`, or nothing for a keyless local server |
| `openai` | OpenAI chat-completions | `https://api.openai.com/v1` | `api_key_env`, or nothing for a keyless local server |
| `openai-compatible` | OpenAI chat-completions | — | `api_key_env`, or nothing for a keyless local server |
| `openrouter` | OpenAI chat-completions | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | `api_key_env`, or nothing for a keyless local server |
| `together` | OpenAI chat-completions | `https://api.together.xyz/v1` | `api_key_env`, or nothing for a keyless local server |
| `vllm` | OpenAI chat-completions | `http://localhost:8000/v1` | `api_key_env`, or nothing for a keyless local server |

One entry per *wire protocol*, not per vendor — which is why several hosts share a single adapter. Adding a provider that speaks one of these protocols is a TOML stanza and no code.

## setup, per provider

### Anthropic

Reached by `provider = "anthropic"`.

```toml
[roles]
main = "sonnet"

[models.sonnet]
provider = "anthropic"
model = "<the model id your account has>"
api_key_env = "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
```

Needs the `http` extra and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the environment. `base_url` defaults to the public API and only needs setting for a proxy.

### MLX, in-process on Apple silicon

Reached by `provider = "mlx"`.

Apple silicon only, and it needs `mlx-lm` installed. No key, no server, no port — generation happens in this process, which is the whole reason the adapter exists: going through a local HTTP server would cost a subprocess, a port, and a second copy of the weights in RAM on a machine where RAM is the binding constraint.

```toml
[roles]
main = "local-qwen"

[models.local-qwen]
provider = "mlx"
model = "mlx-community/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-4bit"
adapter_path = ""   # a trained LoRA adapter directory, if you have one
```

On Linux or Windows this adapter cannot run — `mlx_lm` is Apple-silicon-only. Use a local OpenAI-compatible server instead.

### Moonshot / Kimi

Reached by `provider = "kimi"`, `provider = "moonshot"`.

```toml
[roles]
main = "kimi"

[models.kimi]
provider = "moonshot"
model = "<the model id your account has>"
api_key_env = "MOONSHOT_API_KEY"
```

Needs the `http` extra. `base_url` has a default and only needs setting for a regional endpoint.

### OpenAI-compatible (including every local server)

Reached by `provider = "deepseek"`, `provider = "groq"`, `provider = "llamacpp"`, `provider = "lmstudio"`, `provider = "ollama"`, `provider = "openai"`, `provider = "openai-compatible"`, `provider = "openrouter"`, `provider = "together"`, `provider = "vllm"`.

This one adapter covers hosted providers and every local server, because they speak the same protocol. A hosted one needs a key; a local one usually does not.

```toml
[roles]
main = "hosted"
fast = "local"

[models.hosted]
provider = "deepseek"          # base_url is filled in from the table above
model = "<the model id>"
api_key_env = "DEEPSEEK_API_KEY"

[models.local]
provider = "ollama"            # http://localhost:11434/v1
model = "<whatever `ollama list` shows>"
native_tools = false
```

A provider name that is not in the defaults table must set `base_url` itself; an OpenAI-compatible endpoint has to say where it is, and guessing would produce a connection error pointing at the wrong host.

## local models, and what they cost you in capability

There are two local paths, and they are different in kind:

* **A local OpenAI-compatible server** — Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp. Ronin talks HTTP to `localhost`; the server owns the weights. This needs the `http` extra (`pip install 'ronin[http]'`) because that is the only place a real socket is opened.
* **In-process MLX** — Apple silicon only, no server, no port, no second copy of the weights in RAM. `mlx_lm` is imported inside the streaming call, so `import ronin.providers` stays free on Linux and in CI.

Local builds default to `native_tools = false`, `parallel_tools = false`, `max_context = 32,768`. Narrow on purpose: base Qwen, Hermes and most local GGUF/MLX builds have no tool-calling head, and promising native tools we do not have produces a turn where the model chats about calling a tool and nothing happens. Without native tools the router puts the model behind a format shim automatically, from its capabilities — a human deciding per-model whether to wrap is a human who will eventually forget.

A build that *does* have a tool-calling head says so in config:

```toml
[models.local-qwen]
provider = "mlx"
model = "mlx-community/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-4bit"
native_tools = true
```

## capability overrides

Any of these may be set per model, and a partial override is merged against the adapter's defaults — a config saying only `native_tools = false` does not have to restate `max_context`.

| key | meaning |
|---|---|
| `native_tools` | the model has a real tool-calling API. |
| `parallel_tools` | it can request several tools in one turn. |
| `prompt_cache` | the provider bills cached prefix tokens cheaper. |
| `thinking` | it emits a separate reasoning stream. |
| `max_context` | context window in tokens. |
| `vision` | it accepts image blocks. |

## prices

`price_in`, `price_out` and `price_cache_read` are per-million-token prices you write in the config, and they are what the ledger multiplies. Ronin ships **no** price table: a hardcoded price goes stale silently and then every cost figure in the session is wrong with no warning. A model with no prices set is recorded as unpriced — flagged, not treated as free.

## verifying a setup without spending anything

```sh
ronin doctor
```

It checks that the configured role resolves to a defined model and that the named key variable is actually present in the environment. It does **not** call the provider: a diagnostic that hangs for thirty seconds is a diagnostic people stop running.
